The Component Head for Serious Organised Crime within the HAWKS, Major-General Hendrik Flynn, testifies before the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry on 5 May 2026. Picture: Alpha Ramushwana/EWN

The head of the Hawks’ serious organised crime investigation unit, Major General Hendrik Flynn, has concluded his testimony at the Madlanga commission of inquiry.

Over the past two days, Flynn detailed evidence relating to the 2021 theft of 541kg of cocaine from the Hawks’ offices in Port Shepstone, KwaZulu-Natal.

The drugs were stolen nearly five months after they were initially discovered inside a shipping container at Durban Harbour.

**[Sloppy security at Hawks offices led to theft of cocaine worth R200m, Madlanga Commission told](https://www.ewn.co.za/2026/05/06/sloppy-security-at-hawks-offices-led-to-theft-of-cocaine-worth-r200m-madlanga-commission-told)**

Wrapping up his testimony on Wednesday, Flynn emphasised that the cocaine should never have been kept at the Hawks facility for such an extended period.

"In my opinion, the cocaine seized in 2021 should never have been stored in Port Shepstone. The crime scene management’s failure compromised the integrity of the investigation and the subsequent theft of the cocaine severely compromised our ability to find the traffickers."

_**Daily Maverick**_ is an [independent](/wiki/Independent_media "Independent media"), [South African](/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa"), [English](/wiki/English_language "English language")\-language, [online news publication](/wiki/Electronic_publishing "Electronic publishing") and weekly [print](/wiki/Mass_media "Mass media") [newspaper](/wiki/Newspaper "Newspaper"), headquartered in [Cape Town](/wiki/Cape_Town "Cape Town").[\[4\]](#cite_note-whatsnewinpublishing.com-4)[\[5\]](#cite_note-Schiffrin-5)[\[6\]](#cite_note-6)

It was co-founded in 2009 by Branislav 'Branko' Brkic, who was also the publication's [editor-in-chief](/wiki/Editor-in-chief "Editor-in-chief"), and Styli Charalambous, its [Chief Executive Officer](/wiki/Chief_Executive_Officer "Chief Executive Officer").[\[1\]](#cite_note-About_Daily_Maverick-1)

_Daily Maverick_'s motto is _Defend Truth_, and it is funded by a combination of reader [donations](/wiki/Donations "Donations"), [grants](/wiki/Grant_\(money\) "Grant (money)"), events, and [advertising](/wiki/Advertising "Advertising").[\[1\]](#cite_note-About_Daily_Maverick-1)

The publication states that [journalism](/wiki/Journalism "Journalism"), in its opinion, needs to do two things. Firstly, it needs to help protect [democracy](/wiki/Democracy "Democracy"), which it says it does by means of a large investment in accountability. And, secondly; it needs to help people navigate life, make better decisions, have better conversations, and ultimately aid people in the pursuit of a better life, which the publication says it achieves by explaining the impact of major events, providing perspective from an experienced [newsroom](/wiki/Newsroom "Newsroom"), and publishing a [variety of opinions](/wiki/Journalistic_objectivity "Journalistic objectivity"), sourced from a network of contributors (in other words, avoiding [bias](/wiki/Media_bias "Media bias") and remaining [objective](/wiki/Subjectivity_and_objectivity_\(philosophy\) "Subjectivity and objectivity (philosophy)") and balanced with what they publish).[\[1\]](#cite_note-About_Daily_Maverick-1)

In terms of readership, the publication stated in 2024 that it had approximately 14.5 million unique website visits per month.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)

_Daily Maverick_ has received many media-related [awards](/wiki/Awards "Awards") and is known for, among other things, its investigation of the [Gupta Leaks](/wiki/Gupta_family "Gupta family"),[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) which won the 2019 [Global Shining Light Award](/wiki/Global_Shining_Light_Award "Global Shining Light Award").[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)

The aforementioned investigation was credited with exposing the Indian-born Gupta family, and former President [Jacob Zuma](/wiki/Jacob_Zuma "Jacob Zuma"), for their role in the multi-year-long, systemic political [corruption](/wiki/Corruption "Corruption") and [state capture](/wiki/State_capture "State capture") that occurred in South Africa, during Zuma's time in office. In 2018, Brkic received the [Nat Nakasa Award](/wiki/Nat_Nakasa_Award_for_Media_Integrity "Nat Nakasa Award for Media Integrity") for his role in the investigation.[\[12\]](#cite_note-sanef.org.za-12)[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) In 2021, Daily Maverick CEO Styli Charalambous also received the award.[\[12\]](#cite_note-sanef.org.za-12)

## History

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Daily_Maverick&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")\]

_Daily Maverick_ was launched in 2009 by Brkic and Charalambous following the closure of Brkic's former print magazines, Maverick and Empire.[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)[\[15\]](#cite_note-15)[\[16\]](#cite_note-16) They started a "daily iPad newspaper" in 2011 to complement the existing website; it closed in 2013.[\[17\]](#cite_note-17)[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)[\[19\]](#cite_note-19) The weekly print newspaper, DM168,[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) was launched in 2020.[\[21\]](#cite_note-21)[\[22\]](#cite_note-22)

In 2018, _Daily Maverick_ launched Maverick Insider, a voluntary membership plan that doesn't have a [paywall](/wiki/Paywall "Paywall") or standard donation request. Contributions from readers will keep _Daily Maverick_ free for those who can't afford to pay.

_Daily Maverick_ hosts articles by _[Declassified UK](/wiki/Declassified_UK "Declassified UK")_, a group of independent [journalists](/wiki/Journalists "Journalists") who investigate [British foreign policy](/wiki/Foreign_relations_of_the_United_Kingdom "Foreign relations of the United Kingdom"), the UK military and intelligence agencies, and Britain's most powerful corporations.

_Daily Maverick_'s [membership model](/wiki/Membership_organization "Membership organization") has been widely recognised as a successful example of the emerging membership trend that invites audiences of news publications to pay to become part of a readership community.[\[23\]](#cite_note-23)[\[24\]](#cite_note-24)[\[25\]](#cite_note-jamlab.africa-25)

In addition to its membership programme, the privately owned publication also hosts paid live events.[\[1\]](#cite_note-About_Daily_Maverick-1)[\[26\]](#cite_note-journalism.co.uk-26)[\[27\]](#cite_note-27) It has received philanthropic funding from the [Open Society Foundation](/wiki/Open_Society_Foundations "Open Society Foundations"),[\[28\]](#cite_note-28) Donald Gordon Foundation,[\[29\]](#cite_note-29) Elaine & David Potter Foundation,[\[30\]](#cite_note-30) and [ABSA](/wiki/Absa_Bank_Limited "Absa Bank Limited").[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) It is a participant of the [Media Investment Development Fund's](/wiki/Media_Development_Investment_Fund "Media Development Investment Fund") South African Media Innovation Programme.[\[32\]](#cite_note-32)

It also produces [podcasts](/wiki/Podcasts "Podcasts")[\[33\]](#cite_note-33)[\[34\]](#cite_note-34)[\[35\]](#cite_note-35) and [documentaries](/wiki/Documentaries "Documentaries"), the latter of which includes _[Influence](/wiki/Influence_\(film\) "Influence (film)")_, a documentary directed by Poplak and Diana Neille, which premiered at the [Sundance Film Festival](/wiki/2020_Sundance_Film_Festival "2020 Sundance Film Festival") in 2020.[\[36\]](#cite_note-36) _Section 16_, which details the online attacks on _Daily Maverick_'s women journalists, debuted at the Encounters Film Festival.[\[37\]](#cite_note-37)[\[38\]](#cite_note-38)

## Funding

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Daily_Maverick&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Funding")\]

_Daily Maverick_ is [wholly owned](/wiki/Subsidiary "Subsidiary") by a [holding company](/wiki/Holding_company "Holding company"), which is funded by a number of [shareholders](/wiki/Shareholders "Shareholders"), many of whom are [non-profits](/wiki/Nonprofit_organization "Nonprofit organization") and [trusts](/wiki/Investment_trust "Investment trust"), which aligns with the publication's goal of continuing to provide balanced, unbiased news. No shareholder has more than 50% ownership of the publication.[\[1\]](#cite_note-About_Daily_Maverick-1)

The largest shareholder is South African non-profit Inkululeko South Africa Media. Other shareholders, with less than 15% of _Daily Maverick_ share ownership, include: KMC Trust, Wolmarans Trust, Polyanna Trust, Bakkium Share Trust, Angel Trust, Noble Savage (Pty) ltd, Tondox (Pty) ltd, Styli Charalambous, Branko Brkic, and Tony Rattey.[\[1\]](#cite_note-About_Daily_Maverick-1)

## Founders

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Daily_Maverick&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Founders")\]

### Branko Brkic

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Daily_Maverick&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Branko Brkic")\]

Branislav ‘Branko' Brkic is a Serbian-born South African journalist, [publisher](/wiki/Publisher "Publisher"), and _Daily Maverick_'s Co-Founder and editor-in-chief - he and Styli Charalambous co-launched the publication in 2009.[\[39\]](#cite_note-39)[\[40\]](#cite_note-40)

In 2018, Brkic was awarded the country's prestigious [Nat Nakasa Award](/wiki/Nat_Nakasa_Award_for_Media_Integrity "Nat Nakasa Award for Media Integrity")[\[41\]](#cite_note-41) for initiating the collaborative corruption investigation into the Indian-born [Gupta](/wiki/Gupta_family "Gupta family") family and former South African President [Jacob Zuma](/wiki/Jacob_Zuma "Jacob Zuma"), known as the GuptaLeaks.[\[42\]](#cite_note-42) The investigation won the 2019 Global Shining Light Award alongside [Rappler](/wiki/Rappler "Rappler"), the Filipino publication founded by [Nobel Prize laureate](/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates "List of Nobel laureates") [Maria Ressa](/wiki/Maria_Ressa "Maria Ressa").[\[43\]](#cite_note-43)

Brkic was a book publisher in Yugoslavia before immigrating to South Africa in 1991. In 1998, he launched Timbila, the former South African National Parks magazine,[\[44\]](#cite_note-44) and co-founded the IT business magazine [_Brainstorm_](/wiki/Brainstorm_\(magazine\) "Brainstorm (magazine)") in 2001 with Jovan Regasek.[\[45\]](#cite_note-45)

Brkic launched the print business magazine _Maverick_ in 2005, launching its sister publication _Empire_ magazine in 2007. Both magazines closed in September 2008.[\[46\]](#cite_note-46) Brkic and his partner, co-founder and CEO Styli Charalambous, launched _Daily Maverick_ in 2009.[\[47\]](#cite_note-47)

### Styli Charalambous

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Daily_Maverick&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Styli Charalambous")\]

Styli Charalambous is _Daily Maverick_'s Co-Founder and CEO.

A regular instructor on revenue models in journalism for the [Craig Newmark Graduate School of Journalism](/wiki/Craig_Newmark_Graduate_School_of_Journalism_at_the_City_University_of_New_York "Craig Newmark Graduate School of Journalism at the City University of New York") at the City University of New York,[\[48\]](#cite_note-48) Charalambous was also a member of the steering committee for the Forum on Information & Democracy's working group on sustainability in journalism. In 2021, he was awarded the [Nat Nakasa](/wiki/Nat_Nakasa "Nat Nakasa") Courage and Integrity Award for his contribution to South African journalism.[\[49\]](#cite_note-49)

Charalambous designed and launched the group's "Maverick Insider" membership programme,[\[50\]](#cite_note-50) recognised globally as an example of a successful membership model.[\[51\]](#cite_note-51) He speaks globally about media sustainability membership models, including the [International Journalism Festival](/wiki/International_Journalism_Festival "International Journalism Festival"), the International Symposium on Online Journalism, [World Association of Newspapers and News Publishers](/wiki/World_Association_of_Newspapers_and_News_Publishers "World Association of Newspapers and News Publishers"). He has published on the topic for [Northwestern University](/wiki/Northwestern_University "Northwestern University")'s [Knight Lab](/wiki/Medill_School_of_Journalism#Medill_Knight_Lab "Medill School of Journalism") and Harvard University's Nieman Foundation for Journalism's publications _Nieman Reports_ and _Nieman Lab_.[\[52\]](#cite_note-52)[\[53\]](#cite_note-53)

Charalambous co-produced _The Highwaymen_, a podcast by _Daily Maverick_'s [Richard Poplak](/wiki/Richard_Poplak "Richard Poplak") and Diana Neille.[\[54\]](#cite_note-54)

With a degree in finance and accounting from [Nelson Mandela University](/wiki/Nelson_Mandela_University "Nelson Mandela University"), he completed his articles in South Africa with [Deloitte](/wiki/Deloitte "Deloitte") in 2002 and qualified as a [chartered accountant](/wiki/Chartered_accountant "Chartered accountant").[\[55\]](#cite_note-55)

## Awards

*   2011 – Bookmarks – Product Awards – Email Marketing – Email Publication – Silver – _First Thing_ Newsletter – _Daily Maverick_[\[57\]](#cite_note-Bookmarks2011-57)
